methods.label: Reduce to an acute angle
methods.explanation: \(\sin(180°-30°)=\sin30°\), so the corresponding acute angle is \(30°\).
methods.levelReason: Applies the basic sine reduction formula and elementary angle subtraction.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task applies a reduction formula to obtain an acute reference angle, cnm_h065, supported locally by the identity in cnm_h064. It does not require calculating the numerical value of sine 30 degrees. Method 1 is retained from xiaoyang111222/cn-math-taxonomy contributors: https://github.com/xiaoyang111222/cn-math-taxonomy, revision 62b341d4b66b175413d6e3f697e37639fd96aa2d, licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/.
limitations: The source explanation is AI-generated and machine-translated, not teacher reviewed.
candidate.changeReason: The decomposition 150 = 180 - 30 and the sine reduction identity correctly produce the requested acute degree measure, 30.

review.mathematicalCheck: Since \(150^\circ=180^\circ-30^\circ\), the reduction identity gives \(\sin150^\circ=\sin30^\circ\). The angle \(30^\circ\) is acute and is the unique acute angle with that sine, so the requested measure is 30.
review.levelCheck: Elementary angle subtraction and the sine reduction formula fit the stated scope.
review.methodDistinctness: One short reduction method completely answers the question.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_h065 fits selecting and applying a reduction formula to the specified angle; cnm_h064 records the identity prerequisite. The annotations correctly avoid claiming that numerical evaluation of sine is required.
